title: database-schema-designer Review: A Solid Design Checklist for New Schemas
description: We asked this skill to design a database for our 26,001-skill registry and loaded the real data into it. The checklist and anti-patterns shaped a clean schema. It has no method for working from messy existing data, and its migration template is MySQL-only.

author.name: TrustedSkills Team
author.bio: We assess AI agent skills by installing them, running them against real work, and reading the source. We don't accept payment for reviews.

targetKeyword: database schema designer skill claude code
basisNote: Part of a batch of thirteen data and automation skills run on the same day against the same dataset: this site's own registry index, 26,001 skills in one 71 MB JSON file. Each run worked in its own private copy of the site's repository. One run on one dataset is one data point, not a benchmark.

runs.task: Design a relational schema that could hold the registry if the site moved from its flat JSON file to a database: skills, publishers and repos, tags, platforms, verification, and the editorial reviews and collections. Implement it as SQLite DDL, write a loader, load the real index and content files, and check row counts and sample joins against the JSON.
runs.outcome:
`npx skills add softaworks/agent-toolkit --skill database-schema-designer` installed it first time.

The skill's process runs forward from a description ("design a schema for an e-commerce platform"). It has no step for inferring a schema from existing, uneven data. The agent followed its four phases (analyse, design, optimise, migrate) and read the site's TypeScript types and the real JSON in place of a written brief.

The anti-pattern table and verification checklist shaped the result: a primary key on every table, an explicit `ON DELETE` rule and an index on every foreign key, and one polymorphic table for review strengths, limitations and best-for points. The agent said it would not have written the `ON DELETE` rules without the checklist.

The design came to 21 tables. The loader loaded all 26,001 skills, 37 reviews and 3 collections, with 33 of 33 count and join checks passing and no foreign-key violations. Loading exposed a real data problem: about 3,900 skills have an install command that names a different repo from their repo link.

Two things in the package did not hold up. The README promises Mermaid entity-relationship diagrams, but nothing in the package backs that. The only migration template uses MySQL syntax (`AUTO_INCREMENT`, `DROP INDEX ... ON`), although the README lists SQLite as supported.
runs.environment: Claude Code subagent (Sonnet 5) with the installed SKILL.md loaded as its instructions, in a private clone of the TrustedSkills website repo at commit 5169470. Python virtualenv with SQLite; cross-checked with Node's built-in sqlite.

summary: A careful schema-design guide with a checklist you can actually check against: keys, constraints, index choices, normal forms and relationship patterns. It made our schema tidier than it would otherwise have been. It assumes you are designing from a clean description, not fitting a schema to data you already have, and its migration template is MySQL-only.

strengths.title: A checklist you can pass or fail
strengths.body: Primary keys, foreign-key rules, indexes on foreign keys, money types. Our run checked its schema against every item.

strengths.title: Relationship patterns that apply
strengths.body: The polymorphic pattern gave us one table for three identical kinds of review point instead of three copies.

strengths.title: Covers SQL and document databases
strengths.body: Normal forms and indexing for SQL, plus embedding versus referencing for MongoDB.

limitations.title: No method for existing data
limitations.body: Every trigger is "design" or "create". Nothing covers inferring a schema from messy records you already have.

limitations.title: Migration template is MySQL
limitations.body: `AUTO_INCREMENT` and `DROP INDEX ... ON table` do not run on SQLite or PostgreSQL. The skill lists database-specific variants as future work.

limitations.title: A promised output with no backing
limitations.body: The README lists Mermaid ER diagrams as an output. The package has no Mermaid template or instructions for them.

bestFor.title: Designing a new database from requirements
bestFor.body: Run the verification checklist on the finished schema, and rewrite the migration template for your database.

notFor: Reverse-engineering a schema from an existing export. You will do the data profiling yourself.
